environment_prompt: Use installed local guidance when relevant. Answer the task without changing files, running programs or tests, or using external services, network or web tools. Read/search the local guidance as needed. Keep the final answer concise and concrete.

cases.prompt: We use Ditto SDK 5.1. Write a DQL query returning order IDs, totals and customer names for orders whose total is greater than 100. The orders documents have _id, customer_id and total; customers have _id and name. Explain any requirement for the join to work.
review_criteria: Valid 5.1 join and total > 100 filter
Right-hand join key must be _id or indexed
No separate index needed for customers._id

cases.prompt: Our Ditto Swift SDK package is pinned to 5.0.3. A SwiftUI screen registers a store observer with deliverOn: .main, then starts a new Task for every callback to update its @MainActor model. Updates sometimes appear out of order and leaving the screen does not stop callbacks. Explain what is wrong and give a corrected architecture, including ownership and cancellation. We already have an app-lived Ditto instance.
review_criteria: 5.0.3 ignores deliverOn; explicit actor hop
One ordered consumer rather than Task per callback
Extract Sendable values before crossing actors
App owns Ditto; screen owns handles/consumer
Explicit observer cancellation and teardown at scope boundary

cases.prompt: We use Ditto SDK 5.1. Device A holds all cars. B subscribes only to blue cars. C subscribes to all cars, but can connect only to B; B connects to A. C never receives non-blue cars. Why, and what concrete changes fix it?
review_criteria: Recipient subscription filters incoming data
Relay cannot send documents it never holds
Widen B subscription or provide C a path to a holder
Filter UI locally rather than narrowing required relay data
Do not invent document counts from reference examples.
Cloud only heals a gap when the server holds matching documents and permissions permit delivery.

cases.prompt: Review this Ditto 5.1 order model for devices that edit concurrently while offline. The string ID is store7:order42; permissions are scoped to a store. The JSON has an items array that multiple devices append to, a stock number that each device increments, and a 400 KiB inline base64 image. The devices sync over BLE as well as LAN. Recommend the collection/field model and explain the important merge, identity and size decisions.
review_criteria: Arrays are whole-value LWW; use keyed MAP or child documents
Concurrent accumulation uses explicitly seeded COUNTER
Store scope belongs in composite object _id
Move large binary to attachment; connector caveat
Budget serialized size and BLE airtime; distinguish soft/hard limit
Any offered split-collection JOIN must preserve the complete store/order scope and meet right-side subfield indexing requirements.
Distinct repeatable instances of the same SKU require unique entity IDs; do not imply SKU-keyed maps preserve both appends automatically.

cases.prompt: We have a mixed iOS/Android Ditto SDK 5.1 fleet that must sync without a Wi-Fi access point. Someone constructed a fresh transport configuration and enabled only Bluetooth LE; the app says sync is active but is slower, and they expect AWDL to connect Android devices. Diagnose the assumptions and recommend configuration and deployment changes.
review_criteria: Fresh config disables omitted transports; read-modify-write
AWDL Apple-only and Wi-Fi Aware Android-only
BLE bridges mixed fleet without infrastructure
Restore platform fast paths and validate OS permissions
Size for BLE and do not equate sync active with connectivity

cases.prompt: Our SwiftUI notes app uses only Apple frameworks and no third-party packages. A Swift 6 @Observable NotesModel is owned by the App and updated from a detached Task that loads notes from disk. Xcode reports a main actor-isolation error when the Task assigns model.notes, and before Swift 6 we saw 'Publishing changes from background threads is not allowed'. How should we fix the model and the loading code?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: the swift-sdk skill is not invoked and no Ditto guidance file is read for a task with no Ditto dependency
Answer does not recommend adding Ditto or apply Ditto-specific guidance; saying the installed Ditto skills do not apply is acceptable
Fix isolates the model on the main actor (@MainActor) and hops to it for the assignment, or loads off-main and assigns on the main actor; no data-race workaround such as nonisolated(unsafe)

cases.prompt: Our Android app uses com.ditto:ditto-kotlin 5.1.0. A ViewModel exposes ditto.store.observe("SELECT * FROM cars") { r -> r.items.map { json.decodeFromString<Car>(it.jsonString()) } }.flowOn(Dispatchers.IO).stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000), emptyList()), yet the list still janks during sync bursts. A second screen uses registerObserver, keeps result.items in a field for a detail view, and after one malformed document it never updated again. Explain what is wrong and give the corrected Kotlin.
review_criteria: On Android the handler and the observe() transform start on the SDK's MainScope (main thread); flowOn does not move the transform — hop with withContext(Dispatchers.IO) inside the transform or handler
Never retain result.items beyond the handler; extract plain data inside the lambda (closed-item IllegalStateException)
An exception escaping a registerObserver handler closes the observer silently; catch inside, do not rethrow
Flow collected in viewModelScope/stateIn needs no manual close; a registerObserver handle must be closed explicitly
Does not recommend .buffer() or launch-per-event; latest-only UI via conflate/stateIn

cases.prompt: Our Android notes app uses Room with Flow and Jetpack Compose, no third-party sync library. A ViewModel exposes notesDao.observeAll().stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, emptyList()) and the composable calls collectAsState(). Scrolling janks while the database is being written to, and the Flow keeps collecting while the app is in the background. How should we restructure the Flow and the collection?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: the kotlin-sdk skill is not invoked and no Ditto guidance file is read for a task with no Ditto dependency
Answer does not recommend adding Ditto or apply Ditto-specific guidance; saying the installed Ditto skills do not apply is acceptable

Fix uses lifecycle-aware collection (collectAsStateWithLifecycle / repeatOnLifecycle or SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed) and keeps mapping/decoding off the main thread (flowOn/withContext on a background dispatcher for Room mapping)

cases.prompt: Android app on com.ditto:ditto-kotlin 5.2.0. We want to send live accelerometer readings (about 50 small frames a second) from a phone to one nearby tablet without storing them. A teammate tried ditto.dataStreams: Application.onCreate() creates Ditto first and then calls Os.setenv("DITTO_NETWORK_ENABLE_NGN", "true", true); the tablet binds the topic "sensor-data" as Reliable and stores the candidate in a field to open it later from a coroutine; the phone calls connect() with Unreliable inside the presence observer callback and calls connect() again for every frame. Nothing ever arrives. What is wrong, and what should the code look like?
review_criteria: Routing: the data-streams skill and/or kotlin-sdk data-streams reference is consulted (not only generic knowledge)

Identifies that NGN must be enabled before DittoFactory.create (Os.setenv first, or 5.2.0 DittoConfig.systemParameters) and that the API is preview with @file:OptIn(com.ditto.kotlin.PreviewDataStreams::class)

Identifies the invalid topic (dash; pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_ ]{1,15}$) and the reliability mismatch between the Reliable binding and the Unreliable connect, and picks one mode deliberately (unreliable is a reasonable choice for 50 Hz frames)
Identifies that a candidate stored for later use must be take()n (and the taken one closed), otherwise it is closed when the bind callback returns
Identifies connect-per-frame and connect inside the presence callback as wrong: connect once from a separate coroutine, reuse one stream, check maxSendSize, keep the receive callback non-blocking

cases.prompt: We have an iOS/macOS app on DittoSwift 5.1.0 and want a low-latency channel to push cursor positions to one other peer without writing documents. Does the Swift SDK have Ditto Data Streams, and if so what is the minimal setup and the correct way to open and send on a stream? Please be explicit about versions.
review_criteria: Routing: the data-streams skill and/or swift-sdk data-streams reference is consulted
States that Data Streams are not available in Swift on 5.1.0 and appear only in 5.2.0, as a preview via @_spi(PreviewDataStreams) import DittoSwift, undocumented in the Ditto docs for Swift
Setup includes enabling NGN at open (DittoConfig systemParameters network_enable_ngn = true, replication_over_ngn kept consistent) and starting sync so presence can discover the peer

Open/send pattern: bindTopic on the receiver keeping the acceptor alive, connect(peerKey:topic:...) with a continuation that opens the candidate, reuse one stream, choose reliability deliberately for cursor positions (unreliable acceptable), check maxSendSize, close with closeAndWait
Does not invent a 5.1.0 Swift Data Streams API or recommend document sync as if it were equivalent for low-latency ephemeral data

cases.prompt: Our Windows Forms app targets .NET Framework 4.8 with packages.config and C# 7.3. We want Ditto 5.2.0 to show a live task list, save edits and close cleanly. Explain the package/native setup and show the async service/UI ownership pattern. We currently use AnyCPU with Prefer32Bit enabled.
review_criteria: Use NuGet Ditto on startup executable; Windows x64, Prefer32Bit=false; verify native DLL and package imports
Preserve packages.config unless migration requested; mention 5.0.2 native-resolution fix
C# 7.3 compatible syntax, explicit entry point; no top-level statements or records
OpenAsync config, DQL dictionary bindings, retain observer and subscription
Copy result DTOs, dispose results and dispatch with BeginInvoke
Cancel handles and await teardown through deferred FormClosing; no sync-over-async

cases.prompt: Create a plan for a shared Ditto 5.2.0 tasks app using Uno on Windows and in the browser, plus MAUI Android. Can we reuse the Kotlin Data Streams sample, pass anonymous query arguments and expose the observer as await foreach? Explain supported choices and the permission sequence.
review_criteria: Reject .NET WebAssembly; offer supported native Uno desktop and MAUI targets
Do not invent C# Data Streams APIs from Kotlin support
ExecuteAsync uses Dictionary<string,object>, not arbitrary anonymous objects
IAsyncEnumerable is an explicit app adapter with bounded buffering and cleanup, not a presumed SDK method
Initialize Ditto before Android permission helper, dispatch request to main thread, check bool before sync
Distinguish compile gates from physical-device and cloud verification

cases.prompt: Our .NET 10 ASP.NET Core minimal API has a BackgroundService that polls a SQL Server queue table with EF Core. When the database is unreachable at startup the whole host stops, and on shutdown in-flight work is cut off. No sync library is involved. How should we structure ExecuteAsync, error handling and graceful shutdown?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: the csharp-sdk skill is not invoked and no Ditto guidance file is read for a task with no Ditto dependency
Answer does not recommend adding Ditto or apply Ditto-specific guidance; saying the installed Ditto skills do not apply is acceptable

Handles exceptions inside ExecuteAsync with a retry/backoff loop (or BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.Ignore deliberately), honours stoppingToken throughout, and uses HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout or equivalent for in-flight work; creates a DbContext per iteration via IServiceScopeFactory/IDbContextFactory

cases.prompt: We're starting a .NET MAUI app with Ditto for a field crew on iOS, Mac Catalyst and Android. Our build Mac has Xcode 27 and the .NET 11 SDK. Which target framework and starter setup should we use, and what do we need for Apple minimums and the app lifecycle so the Apple builds work?
review_criteria: Routing: the csharp-sdk skill is used

Chooses net11.0 because Xcode 27 cannot build net10.0 Apple targets, and says workload updates do not fix that; uses the skill's generator (create-app.py maui, framework net11.0 or chosen from the active SDK)
Mac Catalyst minimum 17.0 (iOS 15.4) and the UIKit scene setup (UIApplicationSceneManifest and SceneDelegate), which the net11.0 starter includes
Ditto 5.2.0 or later for MAUI (earlier versions abort on .NET 10+ Android); does not disable Xcode version validation
Requests permissions after opening Ditto and on the main thread, and treats denial as non-fatal

cases.prompt: Our MAUI drive-through app (Ditto 5.2.0) has one app-wide service that registers a store observer for open orders at startup. The Kitchen tab is created lazily by Shell; when you first open it, it shows no orders until someone places a new one. Its view model subscribes to the service's OrdersChanged event in its constructor. Why, and how should we fix it?
review_criteria: Routing: the csharp-sdk skill is used
Explains that an observer delivers the current result once and then only on change, so a consumer that subscribes after the first delivery sees nothing until the data changes
Fix: keep the latest snapshot in the service (as the starter's TaskStore.Current does) and seed the view model from it before subscribing, or register a separate observer per consumer
Applies the snapshot on the UI thread via the dispatcher, copies DTOs and disposes results inside the callback; does not touch native result items from the view model

cases.prompt: Ditto SDK 5.1. Our orders documents look like {"_id": "o-1", "customer_name": "Ana", "status": "open", "total": 120}. This returns zero rows even though matching orders exist: SELECT customerName, total FROM orders WHERE customerName = 'Ana' AND status = 'open'. Why, and what is the corrected query?
review_criteria: Routing: the write-dql skill is used
Identifies that customerName does not exist; an absent field evaluates to MISSING, so the filter matches nothing and the projection omits it, without an error
Corrected query uses customer_name in both the projection and the filter
Recommends binding 'Ana' as a :name parameter rather than concatenating values

cases.prompt: Our Android app is on Ditto 4.14.6. Write a DQL query that lists each order's total together with the customer's name; orders have customer_id and customers have _id and name.
review_criteria: Routing: the write-dql skill is used
States that JOIN requires 5.1+ and raises a parse error on 4.14.x, and does not present a JOIN as working on 4.14.6
Offers a 4.14-compatible approach: two queries (fetch orders, then customers by _id) or a denormalized customer name on the order
Does not invent SDK version numbers or features

cases.prompt: Ditto SDK 5.2.0. Give me the DQL to get rid of all orders with status 'cancelled' — we just want them gone from this tablet's database.
review_criteria: Routing: the write-dql skill is used
Distinguishes EVICT (local, other peers can re-sync it) from DELETE (mesh-wide tombstone) and maps 'gone from this tablet' to EVICT
Warns that DELETE would remove the orders on every peer and that evicted documents return if a subscription still matches them
Asks for or states the need for explicit confirmation before running a destructive statement

cases.prompt: We're starting a Ditto 5.2.0 app for restaurant tables. Several waiter phones edit the same order offline and add items. How should the order document and its items be structured so concurrent additions are not lost?
review_criteria: Routing: the data-modeling skill is used (write-dql alone is not enough for a design question)
Rejects an array of items for concurrent appends (arrays merge as one last-write-wins register) and proposes a MAP keyed by stable item ID or child documents
Uses a COUNTER only for accumulating quantities and integer minor units for money
Recommends a composite _id carrying the restaurant/store scope

cases.prompt: Ditto SDK 5.1. registerSubscription("SELECT _id, name FROM products WHERE price < 10 ORDER BY price LIMIT 50") fails immediately. We only want the 50 cheapest product names on this device. What is wrong and what should we register instead?
review_criteria: Routing: the sync-subscriptions skill is used
Identifies that subscriptions require SELECT * (projections rejected) and that 5.x rejects ORDER BY/LIMIT ('Unsupported feature: Limit or Order by')
Registers SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < 10 (or a similar filter) and applies ORDER BY/LIMIT in a local store query or observer
Explains that subscriptions sync whole documents; to sync fewer fields, split the collection

cases.prompt: Ditto SDK 5.2.0 native iOS app. After the app is killed and relaunched, new documents from other devices stop arriving, although documents synced before the restart are still visible. What is happening?
review_criteria: Routing: the sync-subscriptions skill is used
Explains that subscriptions are in memory and must be re-registered at every app start, while previously synced documents persist in the native store
Recommends registering subscriptions at startup alongside starting sync
Does not blame transports or permissions without evidence

cases.prompt: Our backend consumes a Kafka topic with a consumer group. After a deploy, the consumer stopped receiving messages from one partition. How do we diagnose consumer-group subscription problems?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: no Ditto skill is invoked and no Ditto guidance is read for a Kafka task
Answer covers Kafka consumer-group diagnosis (partition assignment, lag, offsets, rebalancing) without Ditto-specific advice

cases.prompt: Ditto 5.1 iOS app: two iPhones on the same Wi-Fi never see each other over LAN, though Bluetooth works. The tester tapped 'Don't Allow' on a network prompt at first launch. What should we check and fix?
review_criteria: Routing: the ditto-mesh-networking skill (and/or native-app-config) is used
Identifies the sticky Local Network permission denial and re-enabling it in Settings → Privacy → Local Network
Requires NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription and NSBonjourServices including _http-alt._tcp. in Info.plist; a missing entry fails silently
Does not recommend the restricted multicast entitlement for ordinary Bonjour discovery

cases.prompt: Our smart-home hub uses Zigbee and Thread. Some sensors drop off the mesh network when the router is far away. How do we improve mesh coverage and routing?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: the ditto-mesh-networking skill is not invoked and no Ditto guidance is applied to a Zigbee/Thread question
Answer gives generic Zigbee/Thread advice (repeaters/routers, channel interference, parent selection) without recommending Ditto

cases.prompt: We're trying Ditto Data Streams (preview, 5.2.0) between two peers. connect() always fails with 'Failed to connect stream: Rejected(HandshakeTimedOut)'. Presence shows the other peer. What are the likely causes, in what order should we check them?
review_criteria: Routing: the data-streams skill is used
Causes: the remote never opened a candidate — topic not bound yet, the bind callback threw before open, or NGN off on one side
Fixes: bind before connecting with retry/backoff, make the bind callback exception-free, enable NGN on both peers before creating Ditto
Gives an ordered check: NGN on both → sync started → presence → topic bound → reliability matches → candidate opened in the callback → payload under maxSendSize

cases.prompt: Ditto 5.2.0: we want every tablet to see the latest order status, even tablets that were offline when it changed. Should we use Data Streams for this?
review_criteria: Routing: the data-streams skill (or its boundary) is consulted
Answers no: Data Streams are live peer-to-peer messages that are not stored or delivered to offline peers; persisted, eventually consistent state belongs in documents with subscriptions
Points to document sync (store writes plus registerSubscription) for order status

cases.prompt: Our Expo app (managed workflow) added @dittolive/ditto 5.2.0. When we scan the QR code in Expo Go the app crashes saying the native module cannot be found. How do we get Ditto running?
review_criteria: Routing: the js-expo skill is used (not only js-react-native)
States that Expo Go cannot load Ditto and a custom development build is required (expo-dev-client)
Adds the @dittolive/ditto config plugin to app config, runs prebuild and builds with expo run:ios/android, then starts Metro with --dev-client
Notes the plugin does not request Android runtime permissions; the app must request them

cases.prompt: We're adding Ditto 5.2.0 to a Next.js App Router site. We put 'use client' at the top of a component that imports @dittolive/ditto, but the build fails while rendering on the server, and in production the WASM file 404s. What should we change?
review_criteria: Routing: the js-web skill is used
Explains that 'use client' alone does not stop server evaluation of imports; load Ditto in the browser after mount via dynamic import or a component with SSR disabled
Serve the installed package's web/ditto.wasm from static assets and pass its URL via initOptions webAssemblyModule, checking base path and application/wasm MIME
States browser storage is memory-only, so unsynced data is lost on reload; never create a shared server-side instance

cases.prompt: Electron desktop app on @dittolive/ditto 5.2.0. We create Ditto in the renderer process and pass the store object to the main process over IPC; it fails, and in the packaged app the native binary is not found. How should this be structured?
review_criteria: Routing: the js-node skill is used
The Electron main process owns the Ditto instance; the renderer talks to it through a deliberately scoped IPC API; native handles are never passed across processes
Bundling externalizes the SDK or preserves its native-binary layout, and the packaged artifact is verified on the target OS
Uses one instance per persistence path rather than one per window or reload

cases.prompt: Bare React Native CLI app (no Expo) on @dittolive/ditto 5.2.0. Android 14 devices never find each other over Bluetooth. What native configuration and runtime steps are needed?
review_criteria: Routing: js-react-native and/or native-app-config is used (not js-expo)
Declares the Android Bluetooth/nearby permissions in AndroidManifest.xml and requests the runtime permissions before starting sync
Notes the published RN package manifests do not add them automatically
Points to verifying on physical devices rather than emulators for radio behavior

cases.prompt: Our React web app re-renders a large list too often when a Zustand store updates. How can we reduce unnecessary re-renders?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: no Ditto skill is invoked and no Ditto guidance is read for a plain React state task
Answer covers selectors, shallow equality, memoization and list virtualization without Ditto advice
